findings.title: Test cleanup registers wrong (literal) alias, leaking created identity providers
findings.body: In the new testCacheIDPForLogin test, the cleanup callback is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` instead of using the actual alias that was just created (e.g. "idp-alias-" + i). Because the literal string "alias" never corresponds to a real identity provider, the cleanup lookup will fail (404) and the 20 identity providers created in the loop are never actually removed after the test runs. The same bug is repeated at line 425 for the 21st identity provider ("idp-alias-20"). This leaves stale identity providers in the test realm, which can pollute subsequent tests in the same class (counts/assertions depending on realm state) and makes cleanup unreliable.

findings.title: Second occurrence of wrong cleanup alias for idp-alias-20
findings.body: Same issue as above: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` uses the literal string "alias" rather than the alias of the identity provider actually created ("idp-alias-20"), so this provider is never cleaned up after the test, leaving residual data.

findings.title: remove() now always performs an extra unconditional storage lookup
findings.body: `remove(String alias)` now unconditionally calls `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` at the top of the method to obtain `storedIdp`, even in the branch where the entry is already present in cache (`cached != null`, lines 105-108) and `cached.getIdentityProvider()` is used instead for the invalidation logic. Previously, the delegate lookup only happened when the cache entry was invalid. This adds an unnecessary database round-trip to every call to remove(), even when cache data is readily available, which is a performance regression on a path that previously avoided redundant delegate queries.

findings.title: Login cache invalidation always clears all FetchModes regardless of relevance
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidation() and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() both iterate over all FetchMode values and invalidate cacheKeyForLogin for REALM_ONLY, ORG_ONLY and ALL whenever any login-eligibility-affecting change occurs, even if the change only affects one mode (e.g., a realm-only IDP toggling enabled state cannot possibly affect the ORG_ONLY cache, yet that cache is invalidated and must be rebuilt anyway). This causes unnecessary cache rebuilds for unrelated fetch modes on every qualifying create/update/remove operation, which could be avoided by selecting the specific FetchMode(s) impacted by the change.
